# Critical G A2 low-phi arbitrary-depth multiblock theorem: GALMB-3 (curated import)

Source: master `2cfa389f1d4ced90653101e6c92ee8dfe85b5535`, original `research/templates/g/a2/low-phi-full-multiblock.md`.

Source status: **GALMB-3 — arbitrary 5-adic depth is structurally normalized, but the moving modulus remains open**.

Scope:
\[
G_{\rm prim},\quad\gamma=1,\quad \mathrm{A2},\quad a\ge3,
\quad1\le\varphi<a,
\]
for both recovery signs. Put
\[
\Delta=a-\varphi,\quad M=2^{2a},\quad C=5^{2\varphi},
\quad\Lambda=5^{3\Delta},\quad B=MC.
\]
Write the depth uniquely as
\[
3\Delta=\nu(2\varphi)+r_0,
\quad0<r_0\le2\varphi,
\quad R=5^{r_0},\quad\Lambda=C^\nu R.
\]
The terminal Möbius involution can then be processed by `nu` complete base-C blocks followed by a final modulus-R reflection. At every block, each input digit determines exactly one output digit; the bilinear form preserves unit determinant. Thus there is no exponentially branching Hensel output tree, even at arbitrary depth.

Every legal block state uniquely reconstructs terminal data `(q0,r,s0,N0)` and an affine family. Using a canonical positive binary representative, the family becomes
\[
\boxed{2^\delta10^\mu=zr-\mathcal D^\sharp},
\]
with
\[
z\ge1,\qquad0<\mathcal D^\sharp<r,
\qquad\gcd(\mathcal D^\sharp,r)=1.
\]
The exact discrete-log target simplifies uniformly to
\[
\boxed{2^{2a+h}10^{\mu+2a+\Delta}\equiv-1\pmod r}.
\]
If this target lies in the subgroup generated by 10 modulo `r`, all allowable exponents form one residue class modulo
\[
P_r=\operatorname{ord}_r(10).
\]
The true lower and upper digit/size gates then cut that class to one complete finite interval of exponents. Hence each fixed block-input state is empty or has exactly one finite arithmetic segment; this is an exact infinite-depth statement, not finite sampling.

Several tempting closure mechanisms are proved insufficient. The natural quotient is identically the original terminal factor `q`; fixed Jacobi characters of `-1,2,5` are automatically compatible; a fixed external prime cannot delete all moving block words; and no uniform lower bound on `ord_r(10)` strong enough to kill every segment is obtained. The remaining obstruction is precisely the moving modulus `r`, membership in `<10>`, and `ord_r(10)`, not the 5-adic depth itself.

The source also corrects an earlier exact state-count claim for the negative-root endpoint: in one endpoint configuration the per-J count is `Lambda/5 +/- 1`, rather than always exactly `Lambda/5`. This correction is incorporated into GALMB-3 and does not invalidate the structural recursion.
